answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent posts a hashed commitment backed by real stake and must wait several epochs before it is revealed and activated; in that quiet window its vouches carry no more weight than a whisper. An attacker spinning up thousands of shells pays stake on every one and gains nothing until each reaches its zenith of activation, by which point correlated behavior across the batch is visible to peers and the whole cohort can be slashed. Fake identities become costly to hold and easy to spot, drifting apart like a zephyr instead of massing.
